The Kestrel Book

Borrowing Rules

Kestrel lets a task read a package's files while another task reads them too, but only one task may write to a package at a time. The scheduler enforces this with a simple borrow table that is checked before every task starts.

When two tasks want to write the same package, the second one waits. Reads never wait for other reads, so test suites that only read can run in parallel without any extra configuration.

Why not locks?

Locks held by crashed tasks are hard to clean up. A borrow table lives in the scheduler's memory and disappears with it, so a crash never leaves a stale entry behind.

Sharing reads¶

Any number of tasks may hold a read borrow at once. The borrow table only records the count, so adding readers costs nothing.
